body:
Closes https://github.com/duckdblabs/duckdb-internal/issues/11281

PR from https://github.com/duckdb-bot/duckdb/pull/107

Updating a `VARIANT` column with a nested JSON constant took time quadratic in the nesting depth, and deeper values failed with `VARIANT exceeds maximum recursion depth of 128`. Inserting the same value was not affected.

The optimizer folds the cast into a `VARIANT` constant. `RelationStatisticsHelper` then named each projection, group and aggregate column with `GetName()`, and for an unaliased constant that renders the value through `Value::ToSQLString`. Nothing reads these names except `RelationManager::PrintRelationStats`, and nothing calls that. This PR passes an empty `Identifier()` at the three call sites instead.

At 64 levels, the `UPDATE` drops from ~11 s to 0.03 s on a release build. The segfault in the JSON → VARIANT cast reported in the issue does not reproduce on `main` anymore.

Tests:
- `test/optimizer/relation_statistics.cpp`: calls the projection and aggregate statistics helpers directly with a 1,000-level constant, and runs `UPDATE`, `first()`, `GROUP BY` and `INSERT ... SELECT` with it. The SQL test is skipped in debug builds, because `LogicalOperator::Verify` renders every plan expression there and fails at this depth.
- `test/issues/general/test_25967.test`: the `UPDATE` from the issue, kept shallow enough for debug builds.

Not in this PR: `EXPLAIN` and profiling still render the constant, so they are still slow on these values and fail on very deep ones.
title: Stop rendering expressions as SQL to name relation statistics columns
